parsed.doc_summary: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (SB 567 version, operative 2024-04-01, sunsets 2030-01-01): statewide rent cap of 5% + CPI or 10%, whichever is lower, with exemptions. It does not bar local rent control.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, and no more than twice in that period. New tenancies may start at any rent. Exempt: affordable/deed-restricted housing, dormitories, housing under stricter local rent control, housing with a certificate of occupancy within the past 15 years, certain separately alienable properties, and owner-occupied duplexes.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.effective_date_note: Current version (SB 567) effective 2024-01-01 and operative 2024-04-01 by its own provisions; original rent cap applied to increases on or after 2019-03-15 (mobilehomes 2021-02-18).
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental housing statewide, except exempt categories.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable property (e.g. single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, with required notice; duplex where owner occupies one unit; mobilehome owners.
rules.interaction: Yields to local rent control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap. Does not expand or limit local authority under Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (Costa-Hawkins).
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, damages equal to the overcharge (up to 3x if willful), and attorney's fees. Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel may enforce.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condos not owned by REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC
